title: fix(plugin-timeline,plugin-list,plugin-map,components): five more page blocks re-read on the data-invalidation bus (objectui#10623)
body:
Fixes #10623

Clause-②: no

Five readers begin honouring the published data-invalidation contract; no export, schema or accept set moves.

## What changed

Each renderer's fetch effect now names the `useDataInvalidation` nonce for the object it reads, the objectui#10494 shape. There is no host counter prop, no relay and no `key=` remount. An unscoped change (`'*'`) matches too, and a change to another object does not.

| block | file | object the nonce keys on | subscribed only when |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `object-timeline` | `plugin-timeline/src/ObjectTimeline.tsx` | `schema.objectName` (what `find` names) | no authored `items`, host `data` or `bind` rows |
| `object-gallery` | `plugin-list/src/ObjectGallery.tsx` | `schema.objectName` | no host `data`, authored `data` or `bind` rows |
| `object-map` | `plugin-map/src/ObjectMap.tsx` | the `object` provider's object (`dataObjectName`) | the `object` provider and no host `data` prop |
| `element:number` | `components/src/renderers/basic/elements.tsx` (`ElementNumberRenderer`) | `properties.object` | an adapter and an `aggregate` are present |
| `element:repeater` | `components/src/renderers/basic/data-list.tsx` (`RepeaterRenderer`) | `properties.object` | an adapter with `find` is present |

`object-map` needed more than the nonce, and its fetch effect now answers the bus the way `ObjectGantt`'s `reload` does (objectui#10494, objectui#7237, objectui#10578). Four mechanisms, each pinned in `ObjectMap.busReread-10623.test.tsx`:

- **A. A silent run is a re-read of the query on screen.** The map's loading gate unmounts `MapGL` for the length of a fetch, and `MapGL` reads its camera once, at mount. A run is silent (no loading gate, so the map and the user's camera stay) only when the nonce moved since the effect's last run AND the run's query inputs equal, value for value, the inputs whose rows were last committed. So a query change always goes through the gate and re-fits the camera, even when a bus event lands in the same commit. A bus event before the first rows, or after a query other than the one on screen failed, is loud too, because nothing on screen answers that query yet. This is `ObjectGantt`'s split between its silent reload (same query) and its reported one (changed query). One difference: the gantt keeps its chart mounted through a changed query too (objectui#7237), and the map deliberately does not, because remounting is how its camera re-fits.
- **B. Only the newest run commits.** A sequence ref with an `isCurrent()` check, as in `ObjectGantt`'s `reloadSeqRef`, guards every write of rows, the error and the loading flag. The effect's cleanup advances the sequence, so a run superseded by a re-run, or outliving an unmount, commits nothing. Before this change the effect had no cleanup, no cancelled flag and no sequence, so a slow older answer overwrote a newer one.
- **C. A failed silent run keeps the map.** It keeps the last good rows and the mounted map, and logs `[ObjectMap] Failed to refresh data:` to the console, which is exactly what `ObjectGantt`'s silent reload does on failure (`[ObjectGantt] Failed to refresh data:`). The gantt shows no toast or notice for it, so neither does the map. A failed loud run is reported on the error screen, as before, but only when it is the newest run.
- **D. Committed rows clear the error.** Every commit goes through one helper that writes the rows, the ceiling and `setError(null)`. The error is cleared when the current run commits, never when a run starts, which is objectui#10578's rule on `ObjectGantt`, for the reason that PR measured. Before this change nothing ever cleared the map's error.

The `initialViewState` docblock was reworded to match.

## Census (H1): real `SchemaRenderer` and registrations over a counting fake data source

The probe was temporary and has been deleted. It ran one mount per block with the `AdapterCtx` provider around the tree. It read the counts at mount, after `notifyDataChanged({ objectName: '*' })`, after an event naming ANOTHER object (the negative control), and after an event naming the block's own object. A read is one `find` or `aggregate` call.

| block | base `d583db11b` | head (`008a5df9d`, and again at `cef514df8`) |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `object-timeline` | 1 → 1 → 1 → 1 | 1 → 2 → 2 → 3 |
| `object-gallery` | 1 → 1 → 1 → 1 | 1 → 2 → 2 → 3 |
| `object-map` | 2 → 2 → 2 → 2 | 2 → 3 → 3 → 4 |
| `element:number` | 1 → 1 → 1 → 1 | 1 → 2 → 2 → 3 |
| `element:repeater` | 1 → 1 → 1 → 1 | 1 → 2 → 2 → 3 |
| control `object-grid` | 1 → 2 → 2 → 3 | 1 → 2 → 2 → 3 |

## The dispatch hypotheses

- **H2, the idiom.** The call shape is the one `ObjectGrid` and `ObjectChart` use: `useDataInvalidation(fetchesForItself ? object : undefined)`, with the nonce in the fetch effect's dependency list. `useDataInvalidation(undefined)` and `useDataInvalidation('')` add no listener, because the hook's effect returns early on a falsy name. The nonce therefore stays `0`, and a block with no object binding never re-runs its effect. Each pin's static-rows case measures this (0 reads before and after a `'*'` event).
- **H3, `object-map`'s two reads on mount.** It is a double fetch, measured with the probe above. Without a lookup field the two calls are the same query: `find task` with `$top` 2001, twice. With a lookup field the first call carries no `$expand` and the second carries `$expand: ['owner']`. The fetch effect keys on `objectSchema`, which lands after the first query. That is the ungated shape objectui#7895 and objectui#7903 removed from the timeline and the gallery. The nonce neither causes nor cures it: the bus adds exactly one query in both variants (2 → 3). Round 2's sequence guard does not change the count either (still 2 calls at `cef514df8`); when the second run starts before the first answer lands, that answer is now discarded instead of painted. It is recorded as a finding for the seat and is not fixed here; carrier: card to be filed by the seat.
- **H4, refresh in place.** No block changes a `key=`. The pins measure that the same DOM node survives on the two blocks with local state: the timeline canvas (`timeline-canvas`, so its scroll survives) and the map (the `MapGL` node, so its camera survives, on a failed re-read as well as a successful one). The gallery pin collapses a group, fires the event, sees the renamed card, and sees the group still collapsed.
- **H5, pins.** There is one census file per package, following the sibling's reason: a single cross-package file would import packages its own package does not declare. Each file carries a positive control, which is a bare `useDataInvalidation` reader mounted beside the block that must read `1` after the event, and the negative control of an event naming another object.
- **H6, published prose.** No sentence is falsified. The READMEs of the four packages have no sentence about refresh or invalidation. The docs pages (`plugin-map.mdx`, `plugin-timeline.mdx`, `guide/slotted-pages.md`, `guide/architecture-overview.md`) make no claim this change moves. The pending changesets that mention the bus (`10035-*`, `flow-resume-result-5417`, `7237-gantt-refresh-in-place`, `10578-gantt-error-clears`, `10184-*`, `10059-*`) make no claim about these five blocks that this change moves either. `flow-resume-result-5417`'s "Everything mounted refetches in place" is closer to true after this change, not further from it. No dated note was needed.

## Tests, round 1

All of the following ran at `008a5df9d`, unless a line says otherwise. Round 2 re-ran what it touched; see the next section.

- Dependency closure: `turbo run build --concurrency=2` with a `--filter=PKG^...` for each of the four packages exits 0 (13 tasks).
- `type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) exits 0 for plugin-timeline, plugin-list, plugin-map and components. `--listFiles` counts each new pin as a program input once per package (1/1/1/1).
- Whole package suites, run as `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/PKG/` under the verify lock:
  - plugin-timeline: `Test Files 30 passed (30)`, `Tests 341 passed (341)`.
  - plugin-list: `Test Files 95 passed (95)`, `Tests 1134 passed (1134)`.
  - plugin-map: `Test Files 29 passed (29)`, `Tests 173 passed (173)`.
  - components: `Test Files 306 passed | 1 skipped (307)`, `Tests 3022 passed | 17 skipped (3039)`.
- New pins, shown red on base and green on head. The four files were copied onto a `d583db11b` worktree, where they gave `Tests 11 failed | 5 passed (16)`. Every failure is the missing re-read ("expected to be called 2 times, but got 1 times" / "expected +0 to be 1"; in the components file's new-data case, the new row never appears). In each failing case that mounts the positive control, the control had already read `1`; the new-data case mounts none. The 5 passes are the static-rows cases, which assert no read either way. On head the result is `Tests 16 passed (16)`.
- Ablation, with the fix committed. Mutations went through `ablation-replace.mjs` with a trap that restores from `HEAD` by absolute path. Nothing involves `dist`: each pin imports its subject through a relative path.
  - Nonce leg: `, invalidationNonce]` was dropped from all five dependency lists. The on-disk count went 1 → 0 in each file, and the result was `Tests 11 failed | 5 passed (16)`: every block's re-read cases went red.
  - Map silent leg: `if (!silent) setLoading(true);` became `if (silent || !silent) setLoading(true);`. The on-disk count went 1 → 0, the marker count 0 → 1, and the result was `Tests 1 failed | 15 passed (16)`, with exactly "the re-read unmounted the map". A first attempt at this leg used the replacement `setLoading(true);`. The tool refused it (the replacement is a substring of the anchor, so its count cannot rise), restored the file, and ran no tests. It is not counted.
  - After both legs, all five blobs equal `HEAD` and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
- Gates, all exit 0: `check-changeset-presence` ("9 source file(s) of 4 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)"), `check:new-line-citations`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check:phantom-deps`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit` and `check:vi-mock-override-shape`. `check-governed-queue-guard --test` answers NOT GOVERNED.
- Lint: targeted `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the 9 touched `.ts`/`.tsx` files gives 0 errors. For the five source files, the per-rule warning counts are identical on base and head. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` and `pnpm test` are left to CI.
- `git merge-tree` against origin/main `f99f9cde7` is clean, and none of the 11 commits main gained since the base touch these files.

## Round 2 (contract review of the map's silent re-read)

The review failed the map's round-1 silent re-read: silence was decided from the nonce alone, the effect had no stale guard, a failed silent run unmounted the map through the error screen, and nothing cleared the error. Round 2 changes only `ObjectMap.tsx`, adds `ObjectMap.busReread-10623.test.tsx`, and corrects the changeset. The four fixes are described under "What changed".

All of the following ran at `cef514df8`. The pins, the ablations, the build, the type-check and the suite ran under the verify lock (`VERDICT command-exit 0`, held 200s, shared box). The gates, the lint and the census probe ran outside it.

- **Pins, red then green.** `ObjectMap.busReread-10623.test.tsx` has 8 cases: the control (a plain query change mounts a new map fitted to the new rows), A (a query change in the same commit as a bus event re-fits), three for B (a slow older answer does not overwrite a newer one; a slow older failure does not show the error screen; a superseded answer does not release the loading gate), C (a failed bus re-read keeps the rows and the same map node, and logs), and two for D (a later query that succeeds clears the error; a bus re-read after a reported failure goes through the gate and clears it).
  - On `008a5df9d`: `Tests 7 failed | 1 passed (8)`. The one pass is the control. Every failure is the fault named in its case.
  - On `cef514df8`: all 8 pass.
- **Census pins, base and head.** The plugin-map and plugin-timeline census pins (`*.invalidationRefetch-10623.test.tsx`) on `d583db11b` give `Tests 4 failed | 2 passed (6)`; the passes are the static-rows cases. At `cef514df8` those two files plus the round-2 file give `Test Files 3 passed (3)`, `Tests 14 passed (14)`. The census probe (temporary, deleted; run unlocked at `--maxWorkers=1`) re-run at `cef514df8` reads the same as the table above for all six rows.
- **Per-hunk ablation**, each through `ablation-replace.mjs` with a trap restoring from `HEAD` by absolute path. Each leg's anchor count went 1 → 0 and its marker count 0 → 1 on disk, and each restore left the blob equal to `HEAD` with `git diff HEAD` empty. Run over the round-2 file and the round-1 map pin (11 tests):
  - A (silence from the nonce alone): `Tests 1 failed | 10 passed (11)`, the A case.
  - B (`isCurrent` always true): `Tests 3 failed | 8 passed (11)`, the three B cases.
  - C (a failed silent run reports): `Tests 1 failed | 10 passed (11)`, the C case.
  - D (no error clear on commit): `Tests 2 failed | 9 passed (11)`, the two D cases.
- **plugin-map.** The dependency-closure build gives `Tasks: 13 successful, 13 total`. `type-check` exits 0, and `--listFiles` counts the new pin once. The whole suite gives `Test Files 30 passed (30)`, `Tests 181 passed (181)`.
- **Gates**, all exit 0: `check-changeset-presence` ("10 source file(s) of 4 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)"), `check-changeset-no-major`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations` ("0 new citation(s)"), `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:phantom-deps`, `check:test-path-roots` and `check:vi-mock-specifiers/inherit/override-shape`. `check:changeset-claims` lists four pending changesets that name files this PR edits (`6726-*`, `6783-*`, `6939-*`, `9618-*`). I re-read each paragraph, and none is made false.
- **Lint.** Targeted `eslint --no-inline-config` gives 0 errors on `ObjectMap.tsx` and on the new pin. `ObjectMap.tsx` has the same per-rule warning counts as on `008a5df9d` (13 `no-explicit-any`). The first draft of the pin had 2 errors (`rules-of-hooks` in the map stub, `react-hooks/globals` in the host); the harness was reworked before the red and green readings above were taken.
- **Changeset.** The second sentence now reads: "These blocks read neither `onMutation` nor the bus, so any write — through the data source or past it (a page action over raw HTTP, a flow, a server action) — showed only when something remounted them." On `d583db11b`, `onMutation` appears 0 times in each of the five files; the control is `ListView.tsx` with 3. The map bullet now says what a failed re-read does and names the two older faults fixed here. The timeline bullet is scoped to "while the re-read runs", because a failed re-read still shows the error screen (see the timeline finding under Acceptance notes).
- **Main.** `git merge-tree` against a freshly fetched origin/main (`785d3a731`, 16 commits past the base) is clean, and none of those commits touches this PR's files, so no merge was made.

## Acceptance notes

- `element:number` shows its `…` placeholder, and `element:repeater` its `Loading…` line, for the length of a re-read. Neither holds local state, so nothing is lost, but the list is swapped out briefly. Same shape as the sibling's calendar note.
- `object-timeline` and `object-gallery` show their placeholder during a re-read only when they have no rows yet. Otherwise the canvas and the card grid stay mounted.
- `object-map`'s stale-answer guard and error clear are fixed here (round 2, B and D). Both faults predate this PR, and both are pinned red on `008a5df9d` and green on `cef514df8`.
- `object-timeline` never clears `error`, and its error screen is an early return above the canvas. So a failed re-read replaces the canvas with the error screen, and a later re-read that succeeds leaves it there until a remount. A temporary probe measured it at `cef514df8` through the real registration: after a failing bus re-read the canvas is gone and the error shows; after a succeeding one (3 `find` calls in all) the error still shows. The mechanism predates this PR, and this PR widens its reach, since a bus event can now trigger the re-read. Not fixed here; carrier: card to be filed by the seat.
- `element:repeater`'s effect reads `properties.sort` but does not list it as a dependency. Read from the source, not measured. Carrier: card to be filed by the seat.
